title: Integral scalar extension along a finite extension of l-adic fields
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E\subset L$ finite extensions of $\Ql$ ($L$ finite over $\Ql$, $E$ a subfield of $L$ containing $\Ql$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E,\mathcal O_L$, uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ and finite coefficient rings $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, $A_{L,m}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m$ ($m\geq1$). The restriction of $|\cdot|_L$ to $E$ is an absolute value extending $|\cdot|_\ell$, hence equals $|\cdot|_E$ [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]; so $\mathcal O_E=\mathcal O_L\cap E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and $|\varpi_E|_L<1$, i.e. $\varpi_E\in\varpi_L\mathcal O_L$. Hence $\varpi_E^m\mathcal O_L\subset\varpi_L^m\mathcal O_L$, and the inclusion $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ induces ring maps $\iota_m:A_{E,m}\to A_{L,m}$ commuting with the transition maps $A_{E,m+1}\to A_{E,m}$, $A_{L,m+1}\to A_{L,m}$. Let $Y$ be a scheme with small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and for a ring $A$ let $A_Y$ be the constant sheaf of rings, functorial in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For $F\in\{E,L\}$ let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}=\varprojlim_m(A_{F,m})_Y$ be the completed coefficient sheaf with projections $\pi^F_m:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}\to(A_{F,m})_Y$, restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}^F_m$ along $\pi^F_m$ and derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_F)$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Put $\rho_m=(\iota_m)_Y\circ\pi^E_m:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to(A_{L,m})_Y$; then $\rho_m$ is $\rho_{m+1}$ followed by $(A_{L,m+1})_Y\to(A_{L,m})_Y$.

For a complex $P$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules put $P_{L,m}=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{L,m})_Y$, the termwise change of rings along $\rho_m$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], a complex of $(A_{L,m})_Y$-modules. The transition $(A_{L,m+1})_Y\to(A_{L,m})_Y$ induces a map of complexes $P_{L,m+1}\to P_{L,m}$; since $\pi^L_m$ is $\pi^L_{m+1}$ followed by that transition, it is a map $t_m:\operatorname{Res}^L_{m+1}P_{L,m+1}\to\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}$ of complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$-modules [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write

$$
 \operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}=\operatorname{Cone}\Bigl(1-s:\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}\to\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}\Bigr)[-1],\qquad (c_m)_m\mapsto(c_m-t_m(c_{m+1}))_m,
$$

on the termwise countable products of sheaves of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$-modules [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. A K-flat complex is meant in the sense of [def-pc-kflat-complex] for the ringed site $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$.

For $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ with $P$ a K-flat complex of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules with flat terms (one exists [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]), and put $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{L,m}=P_{L,m}\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{L,m})$ (this is the derived change of rings $L\rho_m^*K=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{L,m})_Y$ along $\rho_m$, computed by the K-flat complex $P$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; for $L=E$ it is the derived reduction of [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]). The *integral scalar extension* of $K$ is

$$
 K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L=\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_m\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{L,m}\bigr)=\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L),
$$

and on morphisms it is the induced map. By [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined] it is independent of $P$ up to unique isomorphism, it is a derived limit $R\varprojlim_m\operatorname{Res}^L_m(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{L,m})$ [def-weil-derived-limit] of the tower in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$, and $K\mapsto K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ is an $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$ (with $\mathcal O_E$ acting on the target through $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear]). It is defined on all of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$; that on derived complete objects it agrees with the completed tensor product $K\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ of Bhatt--Scholze (Def. 3.4.10) is a comparison, not part of this definition.

source.place: Prop. 6.8.14 (1), p. 61 (the transition functors D_cons(X_proet,O_F) -> D_cons(X_proet,O_E) of the colimit over finite subextensions, i.e. integral scalar extension, used without explicit construction); Lemma 6.8.2 (1), p. 58 (O_E-hat_X = lim_n O_E/varpi^n); Def. 3.4.10, p. 22 (completed tensor product) and Prop. 3.5.1 (3), p. 24 (completion is R lim of the reductions K (x)^L R/m^n). The explicit formula levelwise modulo powers of varpi_L follows the blueprint: literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-def-sf-operations/def-weil-rationalization-karoubi.md, last paragraph.

mathlib_searches.results: ModuleCat.extendScalars for modules over a ring; no extension of scalars for complexes of sheaves on a site, no derived limit of a tower of derived reductions
no K-flat complexes, no derived limit; for sheaves of modules only SheafOfModules.restrictScalars (ChangeOfRings.lean:36), no extension of scalars

split_report.summary: Lean state none on both branches. Checked against Bhatt-Scholze: the integral scalar extension is the transition functor of the colimit in Prop. 6.8.14 (1) (p. 61), which BS do not construct; the completion formula R lim(K (x)^L R/m^n) is Def. 3.4.10 / Prop. 3.5.1 (3) (pp. 22, 24). Statement rewritten to introduce its own objects: the inclusion O_E in O_L and varpi_E in varpi_L O_L are now derived from the uniqueness of the extended absolute value (lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value), which gives ring maps A_{E,m} -> A_{L,m} with the same m (the old text's 'n large' is unnecessary); the ring maps rho_m = (iota_m)_Y o pi^E_m are made explicit using the functoriality of constant sheaves (def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf); the derived limit is fixed as the explicit cone Cone(1-s)[-1] on termwise products (lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact), as in def-pur-integral-derived-operations, because def-weil-derived-limit determines an object only up to non-unique isomorphism and the old text's 'on morphisms it is the induced map' was not well defined. Independence of the resolution, functoriality, the identification with a derived limit and the O_E-linearity (used by def-weil-rationalization-karoubi) were claims inside the definition; they are now the new statement node lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined. Added deps: lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact, def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear, lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined; def-weil-integral-derived-reduction is kept only as the case L=E. The level-m object K (x)^L A_{L,m} is identified with the derived change of rings along rho_m of lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings (created at the same time by the worker of def-weil-integral-derived-reduction).
